nk-1.1.summary: Phase 1 (The seam). The role table, and every role's executor from settings. See NK1; §D2.
acceptance: The source test fails on a module outside the `kirocrew` executor that defaults a request to `kirocrew`; a test fails when `HARNESS_ROLES` holds a role no dispatch reads; the tests of the four roles that already run on `process` pass with their assertions unchanged; a harness saved for the plan reviewer and for review drafts is the one their requests name; screenshots of Settings › Models at 390 and 1280 px, light and dark, go to the owner.

nk-1.2.summary: Phase 1 (The seam). Output files and snapshots for a child. See NK3.1, NK3.2, NK3.4, NK5.5; §D3, §D4.
acceptance: Tests with a fake child: an output file within its limit is read and validated; a second file, a path outside `.avoozl/output/`, a file over the limit and an invalid one are each refused with the reason; the result file over 8,192 bytes is still refused; a child cannot write into its snapshot; a write root over a checkout is refused before start.

nk-2.1.summary: Phase 2 (Roles with a small answer). The falsifier as a child. See NK2.1, NK2.5; §D2.
acceptance: Tests on both executors: a falsifier's verdict opens or holds the same gate; a `process` falsifier's report with a commit field is refused; it writes no file but its result; with every role on `process`, a task with investigate first reaches Go ahead and lands.

nk-2.2.summary: Phase 2 (Roles with a small answer). The responder and the task summary as children. See NK2.2, NK2.3, NK2.5; §D2.
acceptance: Tests on both executors with a fake GitHub: one reply is posted for one request and none for a blocked result; a reply that matches a content rule is held as it is for a chat; the summary is stored and shown; neither child has a credential or a network path.

nk-2.3.summary: Phase 2 (Roles with a small answer). The issue planner's critique as a child. See NK2.4; §D2.
acceptance: Tests: `critique.md` written by a child is read as a chat's is; a child that writes any other file in the spec folder is refused by its write roots.

nk-p1.summary: Phase 2 (Roles with a small answer). Proof: investigate first with no Kiro Crew chat. See NK1, NK2; §D2.
acceptance: Expected: (1) each worker reports findings and each falsifier gives a verdict; (2) the first task lands, the second investigates again and then lands; (3) every session has executor `process` and no request for `kirocrew` was written.

nk-3.1.summary: Phase 3 (Roles with rules about who wrote what). Plan review as a child. See NK3.3, NK5.1, NK5.2; §D3, §D5.
acceptance: Tests: a child's review with a served model records the round as a chat's does; with no `servedModel` in the definition, or none in the output, the round is skipped with today's reason; a review by the model that wrote the plan is refused; findings over the tool's limit are refused.

nk-3.2.summary: Phase 3 (Roles with rules about who wrote what). The plan answer as a child. See NK5.1, NK5.3; §D5.
acceptance: Tests: an answer of "fixed" is recorded only against the revision the child wrote; a child that changed nothing may answer with reasons only; a folder that fails lint stores nothing and opens the same decision a chat's would; an answer for a spec approved meanwhile changes no file.

nk-3.3.summary: Phase 3 (Roles with rules about who wrote what). The issue planner's breakdown as a child. See NK5.4; §D2.
acceptance: Tests: a bounded issue writes no folder and records its kind; a broad one stores a folder that lints clean; lint errors reach the same session by `resume` and a clean second try is stored; errors left after two tries open one Needs you item; a definition with no `resume` goes to Needs you at the first error.

nk-4.1.summary: Phase 4 (Roles that read a pull request). The pull request snapshot. See NK4.1, NK4.2, NK4.5; §D4.
acceptance: Tests with a fake GitHub: the snapshot holds each part; over the limit the largest diffs are left out and named; the fetch makes no call from the child; the GitHub call counter of RC29 (`radar-coder`, still in force) counts these reads under their own source.

nk-4.2.summary: Phase 4 (Roles that read a pull request). Review drafts as a child. See NK4.3; §D4.
acceptance: Tests on both executors: one pending review is posted with the same body and comments; nothing is submitted; a draft for a head that moved is kept and marked, and posts nothing; a line comment outside the diff is dropped as it is for a chat.

nk-4.3.summary: Phase 4 (Roles that read a pull request). The pull request review as a child. See NK4.4; §D4.
acceptance: Tests: the review is stored and shown; no GitHub write is made; the Kiro Crew chat path is unchanged.

nk-5.1.summary: Phase 5 (Definitions). Read-only roles on each shipped definition. See NK6; §D3.
acceptance: Tests: a definition with no way to write the result is refused for a read role with the reason, and still offered for a write role; Settings › Models shows that reason; each shipped definition is listed as proved or not proved per role class.

nk-6.1.summary: Phase 6 (Notifications). Send notifications from the headless tick. See NK7.1, NK7.6, NK7.7, NK7.8, NK7.9; §D6.
acceptance: Tests: a headless tick with a fake sink sends a queued decision once; with no sink, `status` shows the count and the oldest age; forty waiting items and a new sink give one notification; a sink that throws does not stop the tick or a second sink, and is tried again later; the Kiro Crew push is unchanged.

nk-6.2.summary: Phase 6 (Notifications). Command and webhook sinks. See NK7.2, NK7.3, NK7.4, NK7.5; §D6.
acceptance: Tests: `notifications.sinks` in `.avoozl.json` is refused naming the machine file; a title with shell characters reaches the command as one argument; a webhook to plain `http` on another host is refused when the configuration loads; the payload holds only channel, title, ID and time; a title that matches a content rule is held; the link is the page's address with the page on and the show command with it off; the schema parity test passes.

nk-7.1.summary: Phase 7 (What needs Kiro Crew). The table, and no silent queue. See NK8; §D7.
acceptance: Tests: a `kirocrew` request on a headless tick opens one item across three ticks and starts nothing; Run on from a person sets the role's harness and the next tick starts the session, and from MCP it is refused; a test fails when a module calls a Kiro Crew reader for an operation outside the table; once nk-2.1 to nk-4.3 have landed the table holds the four rows of NK8.4.

nk-p2.summary: Phase 7 (What needs Kiro Crew). Proof: all of Avoozl on a machine with no Kiro Crew. See NK1 to NK9; §D8.
acceptance: Expected: (1) to (5) each step finishes and every session has executor `process`; the pending review is on GitHub and not submitted; (6) the file holds one line per decision and failure, each with only a channel, a title, an ID and a time, and `status` shows nothing waiting on Kiro Crew; (7) the receipt lists each role Codex ran and each it could not, with the reason.
